subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Tech Support Scam
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Tech Support Scam.

hook.text: Your computer shows a virus warning. A number pops up. You call — and the scam begins.

buildup.text: Fake tech support agents convince victims their computer is infected and offer to 'fix' it remotely.

discovery.text: Once they have remote access, they install malware, steal passwords, or demand payment.

twist.text: The fake virus warning was the scam. Your computer was fine before you called.

climax.text: Tech support scams steal over $900 million annually, mostly from elderly victims.

punchline.text: The cure was the disease. Your computer was healthy.

quiz.question: What is typically wrong with the victim's computer in a tech support scam?
options: Nothing — the warning itself is the scam
